news.title: Oil falls on fading geopolitical premium as stocks, gold and copper rebound
Gold rallies amid dip-buying, pared back Fed rate expectations
Oil falls amid recovering supplies, Iran re-escalation fears
This is when you should start buying gold again: BCA
Gold rebounds 3.2% despite a stronger dollar and higher yields.
body: Gold is up 3.2% today, trading near $3,654 after falling more than 9% last week and hitting its lowest level since September 2025. The rebound stands out with both the US dollar and Treasury yields moving higher. A stronger dollar makes gold more expensive for buyers using other currencies, while higher yields raise the opportunity cost of holding an asset that pays no interest. So why is gold higher anyway?

The stock market rebound may be helping indirectly. As AI and chip stocks tumbled last week, some investors sold gold to raise cash and meet margin calls. With Nvidia leading a sharp rebound in equities today, some of that selling pressure may be easing. Gold was already recovering before the US stock market opened, suggesting dip buyers were stepping in early. I’d characterize the move as a relief rally after last week’s liquidation, with the improvement in risk sentiment helping it along.

Technically, last week’s selloff took gold down to the upper edge of a swing area near $3,500. The price reached $3,502 on Friday before bouncing. Today’s low came in higher at $3,533.80, and the rebound has since taken gold back above $3,610.01, the 50% retracement of the move up from the 2022 low. The rally extended to $3,689.47 before pulling back.

For traders, $3,610.01 now defines the close risk. Stay above it and the buyers keep the short-term bias, with today’s high at $3,689.47 the first upside hurdle. Move back below it and the break loses traction, putting today’s low at $3,533.80 back in focus, followed by the $3,500 area that held on Friday.
In the video above, I take a more detailed look at where buyers stepped in, why the 50% retracement matters, and the levels that will tell us whether this rebound has more room to run.

news.title: U.S. Treasury sells $69 billion the two-year notes at a high yield of 4.700%
body: The auction stopped through the WI by 0.3 basis points, reversing the 0.3-basis-point tail at the prior auction. Bid to cover was just above average. The standout was direct demand, with bidders taking just over 6 percentage points more than usual. That more than made up for the shortfall in indirect participation and left dealers with a smaller share than average. The stop-through and lighter dealer takedown give the auction a B−.

news.title: The EURUSD is moving below a retracement target and to the lowest level since April 2025
body: EURUSD has extended to a new low for the day, moving back below the swing area between 1.09041 and 1.09499. In the process, the price also broke below the 61.8% retracement of the move up from the January 2025 low to the January 2026 high. That retracement comes in at 1.09048, just seven-tenths of a pip above the bottom of the swing area.

That puts two technical levels in nearly the same spot. The 1.09041 to 1.09048 area is now the first barometer for buyers and sellers. Stay below it, and the bearish bias remains intact. If the price moves back above that pocket and holds, the immediate downside pressure eases and buyers get room to work back through the swing area. They would still need to get and stay above 1.09499 to take more control.

The session low at 1.08880 is the first level sellers need to get through to extend the move. Below that, there’s little obvious support on the daily chart until the late-March 2025 low near 1.07337. That makes 1.07337 the next major downside target if sellers can keep the pressure on.

When a swing level and a retracement sit this close together, watch how the price behaves around both on a retest. Here, a bounce that stalls near 1.09041 to 1.09048 would show that sellers are defending former support as resistance. A move back above both levels that holds would raise the risk of a failed break and give sellers a reason to reassess.

The two levels serve different purposes. The 1.09041 to 1.09048 area gives sellers a nearby level to lean against. The top of the swing area at 1.09499 is the bigger test for buyers. Knowing which level you’re leaning against lets you define your risk before the next move develops.

In the video above, I take a more detailed look at the break, the levels buyers need to reclaim, and where sellers can define their risk from here. Watch the video to see how those levels line up on the chart.

news.title: USDCAD trades to new 2025 highs and stretches toward the next targets
body: USDCAD is pushing to its highest level since April 2025 as broad US dollar buying and higher Treasury yields give the pair another lift. The 2-year yield is up 9.36 basis points, while the 10-year yield is up 3.4 basis points. Markets are now pricing in a nearly 100% chance of a Fed rate hike in December. At the end of last week, there was still about a 6% chance the Fed would leave policy unchanged.

US stocks are also rebounding sharply, with the S&P 500 up 4.84%, the Nasdaq Composite up 6.64%, and the Nasdaq 100 up 6.84%. The strength in equities is taking some of the immediate focus off last week’s selloff and putting it back on inflation. The jump in the 2-year yield shows where the biggest adjustment is taking place, and that repricing at the front end is helping support the dollar.

Technically, USDCAD has been trending higher in November after spending October moving lower. The pair bottomed at 1.39278 on November 4 and extended to 1.43740 today. That’s a gain of 446.2 pips, or 3.20%, in roughly three weeks of trading.

The broader move higher has come in fits and starts. Since the low around the turn from January to February, there have been several sizable swings in both directions. The rallies, however, have produced higher highs, and the pullbacks have found buyers at higher lows. Last week, buyers cleared 1.42928, the 61.8% retracement of the decline from the February 2025 high to that early-2026 low. Today’s push to a new high for the year extends that sequence.

On the daily chart, the next target is the 1.4401–1.4414 swing area, where rallies stalled in the second half of March and again in April 2025. Today’s high came within 27 pips of the lower edge. After a rally of more than 440 pips, that area gives buyers a place to take some profit and gives sellers a level to lean against, with risk defined above 1.4415.

For buyers, the test is whether the price can get above the entire area and stay there. A sustained break would open the door for another leg higher. A rejection would put the focus on how much of the latest rally buyers are willing to defend.

On the downside, the rising 200-hour moving average at 1.42947 sits just above the 61.8% retracement at 1.42928. The two levels are less than 2 pips apart, making them a single area to watch on a pullback. USDCAD hasn’t traded below its 200-hour moving average since November 5. A move below both levels would break that run and give sellers more control.
As long as that support holds, the bias remains with the buyers. The next question is whether they can turn 1.4401–1.4414 from resistance into support.

After a 446-pip rally, the daily and hourly charts answer different questions. The daily swing area at 1.4401–1.4414 shows where prior rallies stalled and where sellers may lean again. For sellers leaning against that area, a sustained move above 1.4415 would undermine the trade. If buyers break through and hold the area on a retest, the old ceiling can become a floor.

The hourly chart helps judge whether a pullback is starting to change the trend. The rising 200-hour moving average at 1.42947 and the 61.8% retracement at 1.42928 are less than two pips apart. That makes them one support zone. A dip below the moving average can still find buyers at the retracement. A move below both, followed by a failed attempt to get back above them, would give sellers stronger evidence that they’re taking back some control.

In the video above, I take a more detailed look at the daily and hourly charts, where buyers and sellers can define their risk, and what to watch if USDCAD breaks above the swing area or starts to give back part of its November rally.

news.title: Crude oil remains under pressure as demand concerns continue to weigh despite high US-Iran tensions
body: Crude oil has been under selling pressure despite no changes on the geopolitical front. Growth concerns and global stock market rout have been the likely culprit for the weakness as lower future demand expectations naturally push prices lower despite continued supply constraints.

On the Middle East front, Trump said that he favours resuming military action against Iran after the new year if no agreement is reached, while indicating that indirect negotiations remain ongoing but have made no concrete progress.

Meanwhile, Israeli sources reported that Netanyahu is considering striking Iran without US approval, although military intelligence warned that such a move could trigger a multi-front conflict. Israel is also reportedly preparing for a scenario in which the US launches initial strikes without Israeli involvement, with Israeli officials increasingly convinced that a US attack has already been decided and that only the timing remains uncertain.

Overall, there’s been no de-escalation nor improvement in the US-Iran situation as the risk of another direct military confrontation remains high. Oil prices might remain under pressure but we will likely need a bigger selloff in the stock market, an even more hawkish Fed or weak economic data to keep the bearish momentum going.

On the daily chart, we can see that crude oil (CFD contract) is approaching the key 80.00 handle. If the price gets there, we can expect the buyers to step in, with a defined risk below the level, to position for a rally into the 110.00 level. The sellers, on the other hand, will look for a break to increase the bearish bets into the 68.00 support next.

On the 4 hour chart, we have a downward trendline defining the bearish structure. If we get a pullback, we can expect the sellers to lean on the trendline, with a defined risk above it, to position for a drop into new lows. The buyers, on the other hand, will want to see the price breaking higher to pile in for a rally into the 110.00 level next, with the 92.50 level as the first target.

On the 1 hour chart, we have a minor resistance zone around the 84.00 handle. The sellers will likely continue to step in around the resistance, with a defined risk above it, to keep pushing into new lows. The buyers, on the other hand, will look for a break higher to extend the pullback into the trendline next. The red lines define the average daily range for today.
Today we have the US Flash PMIs. Tomorrow, we get the US Consumer Confidence report. On Wednesday, we have the US Core PCE price index and the latest US Jobless Claims figures.

news.title: Gold trims losses amid broad short-covering across markets as growth concerns linger. What's next?
body: Gold extended the losses on Friday but eventually bounced around the key 3,500 level likely due to some short-covering after the aggressive selloff. The precious metal then extended the gains in the APAC session amid a broad-based recovery in many other markets.

The capitulation in the final part of last week seemed to be driven by another liquidation wave caused by the stock market rout. In fact, the US dollar remained relatively flat, real yields fell, and rate hike expectations actually eased following equity losses.

As mentioned on Friday, the hawkish repricing is now over, and we might even see a dovish repricing in the next months if the equity losses extend further and economic data deteriorates. Therefore, the risk-reward for more downside has weakened, although we haven’t got any bullish catalyst yet to position for a sustained reversal.

Today, we get the Flash US PMIs. The data might provide the first bullish catalyst if it surprises to the downside as growth concerns may increase further and rate hike bets further down the curve should be unwound. Strong data, on the other hand, could add some more downward pressure in the short-term.
Looking ahead, gold will likely need support from a dovish repricing in interest rate expectations either from weaker data, dovish Fed commentary or an end to the Iran war.

On the daily chart, we can see that gold (CFD contract) rejected the key 3,500 level as the buyers stepped in to position for a correction into the major downward trendline. If the price rolls over and breaks below the level, we can expect the sellers to increase the bearish bets and target the 3,100 level next.

On the 4 hour chart, we have a downward trendline defining the bearish momentum. If we get a pullback, we can expect the sellers to lean on the trendline, with a defined risk above it, to keep targeting new lows. The buyers, on the other hand, will want to see the price breaking higher to increase the bullish bets into the major downward trendline next.

On the 1 hour chart, we can see the price broke above the minor downward trendline that was defining the bearish momentum on this timeframe. This generally signals a loss of momentum. If the price pulls back to retest the broken trendline around the 3,570 level, we can expect the buyers to step in there, with a defined risk below the broken trendline, to keep pushing into new highs. The sellers, on the other hand, will look for a break to pile in for a drop back into the 3,500 level, targeting a break below it. The red lines define the average daily range for today.
Today we have the US Flash PMIs. Tomorrow, we get the US Consumer Confidence report. On Wednesday, we have the US Core PCE price index and the latest US Jobless Claims figures.
